what_went_wrong: The packet paired tmp/pdfs/erdos1041-main.pdf with arXiv:2603.18757 and tmp/pdfs/erdos1041-revised.pdf with arXiv:2606.24875. Both pairings are false.
arXiv:2603.18757 is 'DA-Mamba: Learning Domain-Aware State Space Model for Global-Local Alignment in Domain Adaptive Object Detection', an unrelated computer-vision paper.
arXiv:2606.24875 is 'A Degree-Four Lemniscate Path Theorem' by Venkata Siddharth Pendyala, submitted 23 Jun 2026. It IS the quartic paper the packet described.
Claude commit 33bee21aad imported both local PDFs under annex slugs named after those false arXiv ids, hash-pinning the wrong identity into the substrate.
Claude commit 7b09f07b95 then rewrote the packet's role text for 2606.24875, which was CORRECT, to match the mislabeled file. That correction pointed the wrong way and has been reverted.
self_error_repair.how_it_was_caught: Reading the erdosproblems.com/1041 discussion, where Venkata Pendyala's comment of 24 Jun 2026 states the quartic result and names arXiv:2606.24875 as its preprint. That contradicted the local file, and checking the two arXiv abstract pages settled it.
self_error_repair.lesson: A sha256 proves a file is the file you hashed. It proves nothing about the file being the work the citation names. Source identity needs the identifier resolved against the publisher, not just the bytes pinned.

sources.citation: Venkata Siddharth Pendyala, A Degree-Four Lemniscate Path Theorem, arXiv:2606.24875 (submitted 23 June 2026)
sources.relationship: the genuine degree-four case of the Erdos 1041 statement; a bounded-degree partial result, not the general problem
sources.exact_statement_extracted: We prove the degree-four case of a path problem of Erdos, Herzog, and Piranian. If f is monic of degree four and all zeros of f, counted with multiplicity, lie in the open unit disk, then two zeros from this list can be joined inside {z : |f(z)| < 1} by a possibly degenerate polygonal path of length less than 2.
sources.exact_locator: PDF p. 1, abstract; PDF p. 2, Theorem 1 and Four-point radial lemma
sources.author_reported_formalisation: The author states on erdosproblems.com (24 Jun 2026) that the result has been formalised and verified in Lean using the Aristotle AI based API, and that he is unsure how to share the Lean files. The Lean artefacts are NOT public, so the formalisation claim is author-reported and unverified here.
sources.identity_resolution_note: imported via annex_import --arxiv 2606.24875; arXiv served this identifier

sources.exact_statement_extracted: Theorem 1. Let f(z) = prod (z - z_j) with |z_j| < 1, zeros with multiplicity. Then there exist indices i, j and a rectifiable curve gamma in Lambda_f joining z_i to z_j with len(gamma) < 2. In particular, if f is squarefree and n >= 2, the endpoints may be chosen to be distinct zeros.

sources.citation: S. Ghosh and K. Ramachandran, Number of components of polynomial lemniscates: a problem of Erdos, Herzog, and Piranian, J. Math. Anal. Appl. 540 (2024), no. 1, 128571; preprint arXiv:2312.13673
sources.relationship: modern treatment of the same EHP lemniscate problem, cited by both local drafts; concerns the NUMBER of components rather than path length, so it is adjacent context and not a direct antecedent of the short-path claim
sources.newly_found: not present in the research packet; recovered from the drafts' bibliographies during this pass
sources.exact_locator: PDF p. 1, abstract; PDF p. 3, introductory answer to Question 1.2; PDF p. 3, Theorem 2.1(a)-(c)
sources.exact_statement_extracted: For monic degree-n polynomials whose zeros lie in a compact K, the paper defines the maximal component count C_n(K) and proves M(K)<1 when 0<c(K)<1, M(K)=1 when c(K)>=1, and C_n(K)=1 for every n when K is connected with c(K)<=1/4; it also records the positive liminf result under the stated regularity and capacity hypotheses.
sources.supports: Primary-source context for the component-count problem and its capacity-dependent results, not a root-to-root path-length theorem.
sources.does_not_support: The Erdős #1041 path-length conclusion, the constant-2 root-pair bound, or any Lean/formal verification claim.
sources.identity_resolution_note: The arXiv abstract page and v1 PDF were opened and compared on 2026-08-26; title, authors, version, date, theorem statement, and page locators agree.

sources.citation: Venkata Siddharth Pendyala, Shortest paths in polynomial lemniscate sublevel sets and a problem of Erdős, arXiv:2606.19178v1 (submitted 17 June 2026)
sources.exact_locator: PDF p. 1 abstract; PDF p. 2, Theorem 1.2 and the introductory definition of S(n); PDF pp. 1-2 distinguish the zero-to-boundary functional from neighboring lemniscate questions
sources.exact_statement_extracted: For monic degree-n polynomials with zeros in the closed unit disk, S(n) is the supremal shortest path length from 0 to the unit circle inside the normalized sublevel set; Theorem 1.2 proves c sqrt(log n) <= S(n) <= pi n for all sufficiently large n and hence S(n) tends to infinity.
sources.relationship: Adjacent but distinct path functional: it joins 0 to the unit circle, not two roots of a polynomial as in Erdős #1041.
sources.supports: An independently authored, primary-source result on polynomial lemniscate path geometry and the exact zero-to-boundary normalization.
sources.does_not_support: The root-to-root Erdős #1041 conclusion, the unrestricted constant-2 theorem, any claim that #1041 is solved, or a Lean/formal verification claim.
sources.identity_resolution_note: The arXiv abstract and v1 PDF were opened and compared on 2026-08-26; title, author, version, date, theorem statement, and page locators agree.

the_gap.found_by: Nat Sothanaphan, 18:49 on 27 Apr 2026, running a standard check with GPT-5.5
the_gap.target: the GPT-5.4 solution announcement posted by kasko37 on 22 Apr 2026 (Overleaf link)
the_gap.statement: In proof of Lemma 6, the subharmonicity is oddly applied to conclude |phi'(r)| <= (1/2pi) * integral_0^{2pi} |phi'(r e^{i theta})| d theta. The left-hand side should be at the circle centre, i.e. |phi'(0)|.
the_gap.assessment: GPT's opinion is that this is not easily repairable.
the_gap.independent_corroboration: Ho Boon Suan had earlier messaged the same exact gap independently.
the_gap.note: This gap is against the April GPT-5.4 claim. It is NOT established here that it is the same gap as any defect in the local drafts.

prior_art_debt_mechanism.statement: the missing citations are attributed to having told GPT not to search the internet, because without that instruction the model tends to see the problem is open and give up rather than attempt it
prior_art_debt_mechanism.why_this_matters: This is a causal mechanism for prior-art debt, not carelessness. The prompt strategy that makes a model attempt an open problem is the same one that strips its literature awareness, so uncited rediscovery is a predictable by-product of how the candidate was produced rather than an oversight to be scolded. Any producer using that strategy owes an explicit literature pass afterwards.
